title: Think it through
goal: I can start a puzzle by drawing it, listing it or making a table. I can read a bar graph and solve logic puzzles.

learn.intro: To start a puzzle, try one of 3 ways. Draw it, list it, or make a table. Then check every clue.

example.problem: Kumar is 6th from the front and 3rd from the back of a line. Count the children in the whole line.
steps: Draw the line. Put Kumar in 6th place from the front.
Kumar is 3rd from the back, so 2 children are behind him.
5 children are in front of Kumar, then Kumar, then 2 behind: 5 + 1 + 2 = 8.
example.answer: There are 8 children in the line.

howto.title: Three ways to start
steps: Draw it: make a picture of the puzzle.
List it: write every case in order.
Table: write what you know in rows and columns.
Check your answer against every clue.

try.text: Lily is 3rd from the front and 9th from the back of a line. The line has {b} children.
try.explanation: 2 children are in front of Lily and 8 are behind her. 2 + 1 + 8 = 11. Check: 3 + 9 - 1 = 11.

items.text: The bar graph shows the books 4 children read. Kumar read 15 more books than Siti. Draw Kumar’s bar on the graph.
items.explanation: (a) The tallest bar is Mei’s. (b) 30 - 15 = 15. (c) Siti read 10 books, so Kumar read 10 + 15 = 25. (d) 25 + 15 + 30 + 10 + 25 = 105.

items.text: The graph shows the stamps 3 clubs collected. Each thin line is 10 stamps.
items.explanation: The labelled lines go up in 20s and a thin line is halfway between, so each thin line is 10. A is 70, B is 110, C is 90. Together: 70 + 110 + 90 = 270.

items.text: The 3rd of a month is a Tuesday.
items.explanation: (a) 3rd to 24th is 21 days = 3 weeks. So the 24th is a Tuesday again. (b) 3rd to 30th is 27 days = 3 weeks and 6 days. 6 days after Tuesday is Monday.

items.text: Each child has a different fruit. Kumar has neither the apple nor the banana. The child with the orange has a name with 4 letters. Wei does not have the apple. Use ticks and crosses in the grid.
items.explanation: Only Lily has a 4-letter name: orange. Kumar has neither apple nor banana: grapes. Wei does not have the apple: banana. Aisha has the apple.

items.text: Draw it. Count the children in each line.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Ravi is 3rd from the front. Mei is last. 5 children stand between them. The line has {b} children.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Aisha is 8th from the front and 3rd from the back. The line has {b} children.

items.explanation: (a) Ravi is 3rd. The 5 children between are 4th to 8th. Mei is 9th and last. (b) 7 children are in front of Aisha and 2 are behind her: 7 + 1 + 2 = 10.

items.text: A café meal is 1 drink and 1 snack. The drinks are milk and tea. The snacks are a bun, a pie and fruit. List every different meal.

answer.text: milk bun, milk pie, milk fruit, tea bun, tea pie, tea fruit

parts.label: c
parts.text: There are {b} meals with a bun or a pie.

items.explanation: Fix the drink and list the snacks in order: milk bun, milk pie, milk fruit, then tea bun, tea pie, tea fruit. 3 meals have milk. A bun or a pie: milk bun, milk pie, tea bun, tea pie, so 4.

items.text: Hexagons are joined in a row with sticks. 1 hexagon needs 6 sticks. 2 hexagons need 11 sticks. 3 hexagons need 16 sticks. Make a table.
items.explanation: Each new hexagon adds 5 sticks: 1: 6, 2: 11, 3: 16, 4: 21, 5: 26, 6: 31. For 41 sticks, count on: 7 hexagons need 36 and 8 hexagons need 41.

items.text:
Which numbers fit all the clues? The number is even and has 3 digits. It is less than 400. Its digits add up to 9, and none is 0. The tens digit is more than the ones digit.
{ll}
items.explanation: The hundreds digit is 1, 2 or 3. The ones digit is 2, 4 or 6 and the tens digit is greater. With 1: tens + ones = 8, so 6 and 2. With 2: 7, so 5 and 2. With 3: 6, so 4 and 2. The numbers are 162, 252 and 342.

items.text: I think of a number. I multiply it by 3 and take away 4. The answer is 17. My number is {b}.
items.explanation: Work backwards. Add 4 to 17: 21. Divide by 3: 7.

items.text: Aisha has $10. A juice costs $1.85 and a sandwich costs $3.40. She buys 2 juices and 1 sandwich. Her change is ${bw}.
items.explanation: 2 juices cost 2 × 1.85 = 3.70. With the sandwich: 3.70 + 3.40 = 7.10. Change: 10.00 - 7.10 = 2.90.

items.text: A grid is made of 2 rows of 3 small squares. Count the rectangles of every size, squares included. {b}
items.explanation: Height 1: width 1 gives 6, width 2 gives 4 (2 in each row), width 3 gives 2. Height 2: width 1 gives 3, width 2 gives 2, width 3 gives 1. In all: 6 + 4 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 18.
items.hint: Count the small squares first. Then the wider ones.

items.text: One of Ben, Aisha and Wei broke a cup. They each say 1 thing: Ben “Wei did it”, Aisha “Not me”, Wei “Ben is lying”. Exactly 1 of them tells the truth. Who broke the cup?   {circ:Ben|Aisha|Wei}
items.explanation: If Ben did it, Aisha and Wei both tell the truth: 2 truths. If Wei did it, Ben and Aisha both tell the truth: 2 truths. If Aisha did it, only Wei tells the truth: exactly 1. So Aisha did it.
items.hint: Pick one child. Are exactly 1 of the 3 sayings true?

items.text: A shop sold 185 pencils in 4 days. Tuesday sold 15 more than Monday. Wednesday sold twice as many as Monday. Thursday sold 10 fewer than Wednesday.
items.explanation: Monday is 1 box, Tuesday 1 box and 15, Wednesday 2 boxes, Thursday 2 boxes take away 10. Total: 6 boxes + 5 = 185, so 1 box = 30. Monday 30, Tuesday 45, Wednesday 60, Thursday 50.
items.hint: Draw Monday as 1 bar. Then draw the other days with it.

items.text: Count the squares of every size in a 4 by 4 grid. Begin with the small ones.
items.explanation: There are 16 small squares. A 2 by 2 square fits in 3 places across and 3 down: 9. A 3 by 3 square fits 2 across and 2 down: 4. There is 1 big square. 16 + 9 + 4 + 1 = 30.
items.hint: A 2 by 2 square can sit in 3 places across and 3 down.

items.text: 9 coins look the same. One is lighter. You have a balance scale.

parts.label: a
parts.text: With 3 coins, you can always find the light coin in {b} weighing.

parts.label: b
parts.text: With 9 coins, you can always find it in {b} weighings.

items.explanation: (a) Put 1 coin on each side. If the scale tips, the light coin is on the high side. If it balances, it is the coin left out: 1 weighing. (b) Weigh 3 coins against 3 coins to find the group of 3 with the light coin. Then use (a): 2 weighings.
items.hint: Put 3 coins on each side. What does the scale tell you?

items.text: Ali has 8 coins. They are 10¢ coins and 20¢ coins, worth $1.50 in all. Find how many coins of each kind.
items.explanation: If all 8 coins were 10¢, they would be worth 80¢. They are worth 150¢, 70¢ more. Changing one 10¢ coin to a 20¢ coin adds 10¢, so 7 coins are 20¢ and 1 coin is 10¢.
items.hint: Try 4 of each. How much are they worth?

items.text: Make up a logic puzzle with 3 friends and 3 sports. Write 3 clues. Only ONE answer may fit. Swap with a grown-up.

answer.text: Answers vary. Example: Lily, Wei and Kumar each play a different game: chess, ball or cards. Lily does not play ball. Wei plays neither chess nor cards. Kumar does not play chess. Answer: Lily plays chess, Wei plays ball, Kumar plays cards.

items.explanation: In the example, Wei plays ball (clue 2), then Kumar cannot play chess (clue 3), so Kumar plays cards and Lily plays chess.
items.hint: Pick the answer first. Then write clues that rule out the others.

items.text: Each dashed line is 10. Tuesday sold {b} more than Monday.
items.explanation: Monday is at 20 and Tuesday is at 50. 50 - 20 = 30.

items.text: In a line, 2 children stand in front of Ben and 6 children stand behind him. The line has {b} children.
items.explanation: 2 + 1 + 6 = 9. Do not forget Ben.

items.text: Lily is shorter than Mei. Mei is shorter than Ben. Ben is shorter than Aisha. Who is the 2nd tallest?   {circ:Lily|Mei|Ben|Aisha}
items.explanation: From the shortest: Lily, Mei, Ben, Aisha. The tallest is Aisha, so the 2nd tallest is Ben.

items.text: Look for a pattern. 2, 6, 10, 14, ... The 8th number is {b}.
items.explanation: The numbers go up by 4. The 8th number is 2 + 7 × 4 = 30.
